observations.title: The recorded pre-existing pinned-sha drift for two files does not exist; it is a CRLF worktree artifact
observations.detail: README §6 / receipt.pinned_sources.drift_note / delivery notes say include/mjwarp_native_probe.h and native/model_probe.cpp were updated by earlier render/volume slices and differ from the pinned sha, and that a full G01 --include-ignored run would expose it. QA recomputation: raw sha differs only because the worktree is CRLF (git index i/lf, worktree w/crlf, core.autocrlf=true); sha256 of the text with CRLF->LF is exactly the pinned value for both files (03151bf5… / 6a01eb01…). fixtures/precision/g01-inputs.json was re-pinned in 61fb6baf (2026-10-26 01:14, message: identity drift 18->0) after the render (d642c039) and model-fields (ef47d450) slices, so the pinned values already are the current identities. The repo's own T4 audit normalizes CRLF (tests/support/t4_evidence/sources.rs:13). Forcing cargo test --test t4_input_precision -- --include-ignored fails 12 audit tests because MJWARP_FROZEN_UPSTREAM_ROOT / MJWARP_FROZEN_WARP_ROOT are unset (panic 'set upstream root' at tests/t4_input_precision/tests.rs:139:71), not because of any hash drift.
observations.proposed_action: Rewrite README §6 / receipt.drift_note / delivery note as: both files are CRLF in the worktree while the pinned sha is the LF-normalized text; git blobs are unchanged since before the slice; the T4 audit normalizes line endings, so this is not an identity drift. Drop the 'updated by earlier render/volume slices' statement and state the comparison basis.
observations.impact: documentation accuracy only; no code, criteria, reference, tolerance or conclusion change

observations.title: Gate clippy/unit do not compile the cfg-gated new code
observations.detail: gates.toml clippy/unit/clippy-cuda use default features and never pass --features native-model-probe; all new modules are cfg-gated and the new test is #[ignore], so the gate neither lints nor runs the new code. This slice has an explicit clippy with the feature (logs/fmt-clippy.log) and the targeted test, but there is no permanent automatic protection.
observations.proposed_action: Add a gate entry (or a registered targeted gate item) running clippy with --features native-model-probe
observations.impact: future regressions in the new modules would not be caught by the default gate

observations.title: Data-frame narrowing uses a bare static_cast with no finiteness/overflow check
observations.detail: mjwarp_native_collision_inputs_copy_xpos_xmat narrows geom_xpos/geom_xmat with static_cast<float> per element, while model Num fields go through convert_f64_to_f32_into, which rejects non-finite values and f32 overflow. An extreme but finite qpos (e.g. 1e300 translation) would silently produce inf frames.
observations.proposed_action: Route the frame narrowing through the same checked conversion entry, or document the different basis in the header and receipt
observations.impact: defensive robustness only; the three fixtures use ordinary values

observations.title: qpos values are not checked for finiteness; nq == 0 models are not exercised
observations.detail: set_qpos validates only the length. NaN/Inf qpos would propagate silently into the frame. For a model with nq == 0 the native side rejects when d->qpos is null, although an empty qpos would be legitimate; untested.
observations.proposed_action: Document that the caller owns qpos validity (or add a finite check) and add an nq == 0 negative case
observations.impact: defensive coverage only; the three fixtures have nq >= 7

observations.title: 'gate ran twice' has only the final run archived
observations.detail: The four run json files under .normify/runs/<task>/ are overwritten in place; only the final-tree run (15:46) is on disk, so the first run cannot be verified from evidence.
observations.proposed_action: Keep both run directories or state in the receipt that only the final tree is archived

observations.title: kind/width mismatch is reported as InvalidDimension
observations.detail: checked_count maps an ABI kind mismatch or a negative native count to InputError::InvalidDimension { field }, the same family used for length mismatches; this can mislead during triage.
observations.proposed_action: Use an ABI-flavoured error or a dedicated variant for kind/count mismatches

observations.title: No cross-check between ABI info counts and collision-inputs counts
observations.detail: NativeCollisionInputsSnapshot::capture validates each field against collision_inputs_info but never compares those counts with the ABI info counts (nq/ngeom/nmesh/...). The test covers this indirectly through the oracle; a defensive 'two count sets agree' check would catch a future model/DLL mismatch.
observations.proposed_action: Add a defensive count consistency check inside capture

observations.title: Summary wording about the 18 pinned sources is ambiguous
observations.detail: README §6 summary says the 18 pinned sources are byte-identical with HEAD (zero change); this can be read as 'identical to the pinned sha', which is confusing given the CRLF note.
observations.proposed_action: Say explicitly 'zero change relative to this slice's HEAD'
